title: Local constancy of the coefficient dual
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a commutative noetherian ring, and $F$ a finite locally constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant]. Then the internal Hom $\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(F,\Lambda_X)$ is locally constant [def-constructible-locally-constant].

source.place: IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf.ihom_unit docstring, local finite presentation and dual finite generation

proof.text: Choose an étale cover trivializing F. Discard empty members. On a nonempty member F is the constant sheaf associated to a module M. A geometric stalk identifies M with a stalk of F, so M is finitely generated. Since Λ is noetherian, choose a finite presentation Λᵐ → Λⁿ → M → 0. Constant sheafification is exact and monoidal, so this presents the restriction of F by finite free constant sheaves. Internal Hom into the unit is left exact: its restriction is the kernel of the transposed map Λⁿ → Λᵐ. That map is constant and its kernel is the constant sheaf associated to Hom_Λ(M, Λ), since constant sheafification preserves finite limits. Restriction to a slice commutes with internal Hom, by the local characterization of internal Hom through maps from restricted sheaves. Hence the same cover trivializes the coefficient dual. Empty members impose no condition.
